narrative:
The 2025 Los Angeles Angels opened the season with flashes of the power and promise that had long been promised to a fanbase starved for October baseball. Logan O'Hoppe's grand slam in the first week, Nolan Schanuel's clutch triple, and Jo Adell's dramatic upheld double against the Giants in late April suggested that perhaps this was finally the year the pieces would come together. The lineup showed genuine pop — 226 home runs on the season — and moments of real electricity that gave Anaheim reason to believe.

The middle stretch of the season was defined by Taylor Ward's pair of grand slams and a Jorge Soler double that briefly made the Angels look like a legitimate contender. But for every surge, the pitching staff answered with a catastrophic unraveling. Shaun Anderson serving up a three-run shot to Shohei Ohtani — returning to Anaheim in a Dodgers uniform — was a gut punch that captured the season's cruel contradictions. The bullpen and rotation alike could not sustain leads, and the run differential of minus-164 told the true story.

As summer deepened, the Angels spiraled. Ryan Zeferjahn gave up a decisive home run on July 2nd, José Fermin surrendered a Kyle Schwarber grand slam in July, and Reid Detmers was torched in August. Each damaging blow reinforced what the standings were already screaming: this roster was not built to compete in 2025. The youth movement — Christian Moore's homer in late June, Zach Neto's clutch single in July — offered tantalizing glimpses of a better future, but it came wrapped in losing.

The Angels finished 72-90, missing the playoffs for a fifth consecutive season. Jo Adell's 33rd home run in September was a bittersweet exclamation point — a reminder of individual talent flourishing in the context of team failure. The 2025 Angels were a team of moments, not a team of outcomes, and the long rebuild in Anaheim continued with its familiar ache.

chapters.title: Fast Starts and Early Sparks
chapters.description: The Angels open with big moments — a grand slam, a clutch triple, and early signs of offensive life.

chapters.title: The Surge: Ward, Soler, and Grand Slam Power
chapters.description: A mid-spring offensive explosion fueled by grand slams and clutch doubles raises hopes of a genuine pennant race.

chapters.title: Pitching Cracks and Momentum Fades
chapters.description: The bullpen and rotation begin to buckle in June, surrendering big moments that erase the Angels' hard-fought leads.

chapters.title: Youth Shines Through the Losing
chapters.description: Young stars like Christian Moore and Nolan Schanuel deliver highlight moments even as the season begins slipping away.

chapters.title: Summer Collapse
chapters.description: A brutal stretch of damaging home runs allowed and failed save opportunities seals the Angels' fate in July and August.

chapters.title: September Farewells
chapters.description: With the playoffs out of reach, Jo Adell's 33rd homer and scattered bright spots offer a bittersweet close to a disappointing season.
